head.title: Concatenative Programming: From Ivory to Metal (2017)
head.subtitle: Stanford EE380 Computer Systems Colloquium Seminar

body.para: “Concatenative programming is a relatively new programming paradigm built on a simple yet powerful tool: function composition. In this talk I will give an overview of concatenative languages from high-level theory down to low-level implementation. I will discuss some historical background, give an overview of the existing concatenative programming literature, then dive into examples of the exciting advantages that these languages may have to offer in terms of program correctness, safety, usability, and performance on the hardware of today and tomorrow.”
